title: Calibrated temperature did not replace timely ozone readings at 30 rural US sites in 2022-2025
abstract: We tested whether temperature forecasts can offset delayed ozone readings. We fitted five-year models with ozone ages of 1, 2, 3 and 7 days, or no ozone. Yesterday weather stayed available. Forecast weather was calibrated with earlier summers only. All ages used the same scored days. In 2022-2025 at 30 rural eastern US sites, the three-day ozone model with 24-hour GFS temperature cut squared error by 12.31% against the same-age reference. It still had 15.89% more squared error [limits 8.99 to 21.73%] than the one-day ozone model without target temperature. Against the one-day ozone model with the same temperature input, its reduction was -41.54% [-48.57, -34.69]. Limits are descriptive whole-year resamples from four summers. A longer 2008-2025 observed-weather test and tests with 48-hour inputs, early temperature slopes and no ozone are supplied. Final data, a selected network, a fixed afternoon mean and unknown archive delivery times limit operational use. This is a data-delay sensitivity test, not a live forecast trial or a causal climate test.
